title: Man. Post. Cap. VIII: Thomas praised; inherent vice; status questionis restated
pass_a_gloss: So Placeus praises Thomas Aquinas's words. In each of us there truly and properly is sin deep in the marrow—not actual but, so to speak, habitual—worthy not only of temporal but of eternal death, which our side usually proves against the Papists with many arguments the opponent has doubtless read and approves. Therefore Adam's transgression made us liable to bodily and eternal death by intervening inherent vice and fault with which it infected us. That vice in Adam natural sequel produced; from Adam into us it was propagated no otherwise than human nature itself by carnal generation. Placeus restates the status of the question here so we keep it purged and clarified always before our eyes, lest straying we fall into empty logomachies.
pass_b_english: So I praise these words of Thomas Aquinas. In each of us there is truly and properly sin deep in the marrow, not indeed actual, but, so to speak, habitual, worthy not only of temporal death but of eternal also, which our side usually prove against the Papists with many arguments which you have doubtless both read and approve. We, therefore, Adam's transgression made liable to bodily and eternal death by the intervention of the inherent vice and fault with which it infected us. But this vice in Adam natural sequel produced; and from Adam into us it was propagated no otherwise than human nature itself by carnal generation. I wanted to repeat the status of the question in this place, because it becomes us to keep it purged and clarified perpetually before our eyes, lest sometime straying from it we slide into empty logomachies.
source_text: Itaque laudo haec verba Thomae Aquinatis. Singulis nobis medullitus inest vere & proprie peccatum, non quidem actuale, sed, ut ita loquar, habituale, dignum non temporali modo morte, sed aeterna etiam, quod nostri adversus Pontificios solent multis argumentis evincere, quae tu proculdubio & legisti, & probas. Nos ergo transgressio Adami fecit obnoxios morti corporali & aeternae interventu inhaerentis vitii & culpae, quo nos infecit. Hoc autem vitium in Adamo naturali sequela produxit; ab Adamo vero in nos haud aliter quam ipsa natura humana propagatum est generatione carnali. Volui statum quaestionis hoc loco repetere, quoniam eum purgatum & enucleatum habere perpetuo ob oculos nos decet, ne ab eo aliquando aberrantes in inanes λογομαχίας prolabamur.

choices.choice: Praise Thomas; inherent vice; restate status questionis
